text:
Nora: FYI — Alpine Retail flagged repeated 500s on Dedicated when uploading large embedding batches. Sales is pushing for a fix in the next 48h.
Sanjay: reproducer attached in support ticket. They're on our dedicated pool 'ded-alpine-2'. Errors look like timeout + OOM fallback logs.
Liam: I can triage. Quick question: do we have a minimal rollback / toggle that avoids a full model swap? Could be batching config that's aggressive.
Maya: From SRE side, we can't push an untested kernel change. Prefer config-level mitigation + soft canary. We have autoscale headroom but latency SLO might breach.
Alex: Customer pressure: they want "no interruption", but would accept short maintenance window if we can guarantee retry/backoff. Sales asks for a comm plan.
Nora: Proposal: scoped hotpatch = change per-tenant batching cap + KV cache eviction threshold. No model changes. Canary to 5% of Alpine traffic, monitor 5m p99 latency and 500s.
Liam: Agree. I can implement the cap change + a per-tenant toggle. PR will be small. Need a quick test matrix.
Sanjay: Support will route Alpine to canary and keep ticket updated. I'll attach list of sample payloads for QA.
Maya: Canary criteria: if 5m p99 latency increase < 10% and 500 error rate drops by > 80%, proceed to 25% then 100% over 2 hours. If any spike to critical, rollback.
Nora: Acceptance also needs no customer-visible token loss and error logs must show the new batching flag. Add code snippet in rollout docs.
Liam: Rollout commands (devops):
```
# enable per-tenant batching override
redwoodctl config set --tenant alpine --key batching.max_tokens --value 1024 --env canary
redwoodctl route update --tenant alpine --percent 5 --env canary
```
Maya: I'll create the monitoring dashboard and an alert: alert if 5m 500-rate > 0.5% or p99 latency > baseline + 200ms.
Alex: I'll draft the customer comm: short maintenance note + what to expect, who to contact. CC SRE on the message.
Sanjay: Support will be on standby during canary and will escalate within 10m for any regression.
Nora: Timeline: dev PR today -> canary tomorrow 09:00 UTC -> evaluate for 2 hours -> ramp. Can we hit that? @Liam @Maya
Liam: yes, PR by EOD, will include unit + integration tests.
Maya: monitoring + alerting ready, ops runbook ready.
deploy-bot: scheduled canary for alpine at 1712434800 (confirmed)
support-bot: ticket #SR-5482 updated with canary timeline and contact list.
Nora: Thanks. Quick doc task: I'll update the intake ticket with "scope-carve" justification and close the loop with sales. :thumbsup:
Alex: Thanks all — I'll send the customer note after PR is merged.
Nora: Closing action items: Liam (PR + toggle), Maya (dash + alert), Sanjay (support coverage), Alex (customer comm). I'll follow up in this thread with post-canary results.
